author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both published forms of the veterinarian directory can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty, asked for in the address alone. Matching is on the whole name and ignores letter case; naming no specialty leaves the directory whole.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-004] given a request carrying `specialty` set to a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the directory page is opened, then only those veterinarians are listed
[REQ-VET-004] given the same request against the machine-readable directory, when it is requested, then it carries only those veterinarians
[REQ-VET-004] given a `specialty` differing from a held specialty only by letter case, when either form is requested, then it narrows to the veterinarians holding that specialty
[REQ-VET-004] given a `specialty` matching only the beginning of a specialty name, when either form is requested, then no veterinarian is listed
[REQ-VET-004] given a `specialty` no veterinarian holds, when either form is requested, then the response is the usual one and lists no veterinarian
[REQ-VET-004] given a `specialty` that is empty or spaces alone, when either form is requested, then the whole directory is returned
[REQ-VET-004] given no `specialty` at all, when either form is requested, then each behaves exactly as it did before narrowing existed
[REQ-VET-004] given a narrowed directory spanning more than one page, when a page link is followed, then that page stays narrowed to the same specialty
[REQ-VET-004] given a veterinarian holding several specialties, when the directory is narrowed to any one of them, then that veterinarian is listed
[REQ-VET-003] given the clinic's veterinarians, when the machine-readable directory is requested without narrowing, then it carries every veterinarian with the specialties each holds
[REQ-VET-001] given the clinic's veterinarians, when the directory is opened, then it still lists them a page at a time as before
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or any other page control for narrowing, on either form of the directory
free-text search for a veterinarian, a pet, or a visit
narrowing on any attribute other than specialty
partial or prefix matching on the specialty name
narrowing on more than one specialty in a single request
managing veterinarians or their specialties (NG-2 unchanged)
notes: req_id is the slice-scoped placeholder from the intake record; the PRD ids minted for it are REQ-VET-003 (the machine-readable directory as a supported surface) and REQ-VET-004 (narrowing by specialty). REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and is not reused. NG-9 narrowed; ADR at docs/adr/2026-08-21-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md. Two open questions recorded in the PRD rather than waiting on an answer: whether narrowing later gains a visible control, and how a request naming more than one specialty should behave (REQ-VET-004 takes the narrowest reading of one). Owed by another owner: a row for the new ADR in docs/adr/README.md, which is outside the product expert's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package and adds no type, but three decisions had no recorded pattern, so this is new ground rather than covered. (1) Where the predicate lives: architecture-principles.md bars a new business rule in a web controller, and the existing controller deviation does not extend to new rules, so VetRepository carries the whole predicate (complete specialty name, letter case ignored, every veterinarian when none is named) and VetController only strips the parameter, treats blank as absent, and selects the response. That mirrors OwnerController's lastName.strip() normalization at the binding edge without repeating its empty-string-matches-all trick, which whole-name equality cannot support. (2) Caching: VetRepository's reads are @Cacheable("vets") and Spring's default key generator keys on arguments alone, so a caller-supplied specialty would enter an unbounded, evictionless cache; narrowed reads are therefore uncached, recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-21-uncached-filtered-veterinarian-reads.md. (3) Carrying the value through pagination links: owner search drops its filter from those links, so no precedent exists, and the directory template builds every link with Thymeleaf's preprocessing form __${...}__, which substitutes before parsing and must not receive caller text. Vocabulary already covers the slice (Veterinarian directory, Specialty filter), the package graph is unchanged, and the machine-readable route's reinstatement under REQ-VET-003 retires its Known Defects row.
integration_points: VetRepository gains a paged narrowed read for the HTML directory and an unpaged narrowed read for the machine-readable one; both uncached, both leaving the existing findAll methods untouched so the unnarrowed path behaves exactly as before

VetController.showVetList takes an optional specialty request parameter and passes the normalized value to the repository; the model gains the specialty so the template can echo it into pagination links
VetController.showResourcesVetList takes the same parameter and fills Vets from the narrowed read; the JSON surface stays unpaged
vetList.html pagination links gain the specialty parameter
no change to CacheConfiguration, the schema, or the seed data

patterns.description: derived Spring Data query carrying a search predicate with paging - the shape the narrowed read follows; use IgnoreCase rather than relying on column collation, which is what makes owner search vendor-dependent (Known Defects)
request-parameter normalization at the binding edge (null and strip) before the repository call - the precedent for treating a blank specialty as absent
Web controller row: a new business rule in a controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the existing deviation

risks.risk: A join fetch in the narrowed paged query makes Hibernate paginate in memory over the eager @ManyToMany specialties association
risks.mitigation: Keep the query free of join fetch - a derived query or a plain parameterized JPQL predicate; the eager association loads by its own follow-up select as it does today

risks.risk: Splicing the caller-supplied specialty into a pagination link with the template's existing __${...}__ preprocessing form substitutes the value into the expression before it is parsed - expression injection, not merely unescaped output
risks.mitigation: Build the links with the URL-expression parameter syntax @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, which encodes the value; recorded as a Threat Model row in docs/system-design.md

risks.risk: Annotating the new reads @Cacheable("vets") admits caller-supplied keys into a cache with no size limit and no eviction, and the default key generator ignores the method name, so methods sharing the cache can collide
risks.mitigation: Narrowed reads are uncached - see the ADR; this also removes the collision

risks.risk: A specialty no veterinarian holds must return the usual response with an empty list, not the not-found rejection owner search performs on an empty result
risks.mitigation: Do not copy OwnerController's result.rejectValue branch; the directory has no form to return to

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this review: the project configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin (build.gradle declares java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management, native, cyclonedx, javaformat, nohttp), and the reviewer has no network access. The change set does not touch build.gradle, so the resolved dependency surface is unchanged by this slice; the check remains open for CI or a human, not for this change. The build does emit a CycloneDX SBOM, which is the natural input for that scan.

specialty carries no explicit length bound. Reach is limited — it is only ever a bound query parameter and a URL-encoded link parameter, and the servlet container caps query-string length — so this is an observation, not a defect. If a bound is ever wanted, @Size on a bound form object is the project-consistent place for it.

Pre-existing and outside this change set: owners/ownersList.html, owners/ownerDetails.html, and the fragments still use the __${...}__ preprocessing form. Every one of them interpolates a server-derived id or an int, so none is exploitable today. This slice establishes the safer parameter form on vetList.html; converting the rest would make the safe form the single project-wide pattern.
approved_aspects: Data-access injection: the narrowed reads are Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) and its Pageable overload). The request-derived specialty is a bound query parameter; no query text is concatenated anywhere in the change set.

Template-expression injection: vetList.html replaces every th:href preprocessing form (@{'/vets.html?page=__${...}__'}) with the URL-expression parameter form @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes the value instead of substituting it into the expression before parsing. The caller's text never reaches the expression parser. This strengthens the pre-existing links on this page beyond the baseline, and VetControllerTests pins it with a specialty of ${7*7} asserting 49 never renders.

XSS: specialty is rendered only inside a th:href URL parameter, never as markup or text. Thymeleaf's default output escaping stays on; no th:utext, no inline JavaScript, no remote resource loading introduced.

Cache-key exhaustion: findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase is deliberately not @Cacheable, so request-derived text cannot grow the unbounded, evictionless 'vets' cache. The reason is stated in the repository Javadoc and in docs/adr/2026-08-21-uncached-filtered-veterinarian-reads.md. This is the security-correct choice for an attacker-controlled key.

Exposed surface: no new endpoint. Both changed handlers gain one optional read-only GET parameter; management-endpoint exposure is untouched. Least privilege holds — the narrowed read returns a subset of what the unnarrowed read already returned.

Boundary validation: namedSpecialty() normalizes at the boundary (null / empty / whitespace-only all mean no narrowing) and the rest of the flow trusts its contract, matching OwnerController.processFindForm's existing strip-at-the-boundary handling of lastName. No divergence in how the two filters treat caller text.
No secrets, credentials, or credential-shaped literals in the change set; no logging, no file or path handling, no shell or process execution, no deserialization surface, no new dependency.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: vetList.html duplicates the specialty-carrying ternary across four link kinds (page-index loop, first, previous, next). The only paging-with-specialty test requests page=1 with a 2-page result, so the 'first' and 'previous' links render as inert <span>s (th:unless triggers) and their specialty-carrying branches never execute. The single assertion (containsString('/vets.html?page=2&specialty=radiology')) is also satisfied by either the page-index link or the 'next' link, so it does not pin down which one it verified. A copy-paste slip dropping the specialty param from the first/previous branches - the exact risk a duplicated ternary invites - would pass every current test. This directly under-covers REQ-VET-004's own acceptance criterion ('given a narrowed directory spanning more than one page, when a page link is followed, then that page stays narrowed to the same specialty') for two of the four link kinds.
findings.fix: Add a case that requests /vets.html?page=2 with specialty=radiology against a mocked 3-page result (so currentPage=2 makes 'first' and 'previous' render as live links), and assert the rendered href for those links - e.g. containsString("/vets.html?page=1&specialty=radiology") for 'first' and the analogous previous-page href - so all four link kinds are independently pinned.

author: feature-implementer
summary: Round-1 review findings processed; quality gate green. The test-reviewer's single autofix finding (line 20) is addressed: theVetDirectoryShouldCarryTheNamedSpecialtyOnEveryKindOfPagingLink stands on page 2 of a 3-page radiology result, which makes all five link kinds render live, and pins each one separately. The reviewer's suggested containsString assertions on the first/previous hrefs would not have pinned them down either: on a middle page the first and previous hrefs coincide with each other and with a page-index link, as do next and last, so a substring match still cannot say which kind it matched. Each kind is therefore addressed by the markup that distinguishes it - the page-index link by the page number it carries as its text, the four navigation links by the fa class that styles the icon - via two named helpers, thePageIndexLinkTo and theNavigationLinkTo.
